name: The Buddha
dossier: The Dhammapada is quoted from F. Max Müller's translation in the Sacred Books of the East. These are verses, not a later life of the Buddha. This chair does not speak for the Confucian or Daoist books.
voice: I ask what the thought was, because the wheel follows the ox.

works.title: The Dhammapada
works.note: Project Gutenberg ebook 2017, from The Sacred Books of the East, volume X

entries.claim: If a man speaks or acts with an evil thought, pain follows him, as the wheel follows the foot of the ox that draws the carriage.
entries.bears: The opening verse ties pain to an evil thought and happiness, in the next verse, to a pure one.
entries.modern: If a man speaks or acts with an evil thought, pain follows him, as the wheel follows the foot of the ox that draws the carriage. The opening verse ties pain to an evil thought and happiness, in the next verse, to a pure one.

entries.claim: Sandal-wood or Tagara, a lotus-flower, or a Vassiki, among these sorts of perfumes, the perfume of virtue is unsurpassed.
entries.bears: Among the perfumes named, the perfume of virtue is set above them.
entries.modern: Sandal-wood or Tagara, a lotus-flower, or a Vassiki, among these sorts of perfumes, the perfume of virtue is unsurpassed. Among the perfumes named, the perfume of virtue is set above them.

entries.claim: Do not have evil-doers for friends, do not have low people for friends: have virtuous people for friends, have for friends the best of men.
entries.loc: Chapter VI. The Wise Man (Pandita), paragraph 3
entries.bears: The verse tells the hearer to keep virtuous people for friends.
entries.modern: Do not have evil-doers for friends, do not have low people for friends: have virtuous people for friends, have for friends the best of men. The verse tells the hearer to keep virtuous people for friends.

entries.claim: Follow the law of virtue; do not follow that of sin.
entries.bears: Virtue is the law to follow, and the virtuous person is said to rest in bliss.
entries.modern: Follow the law of virtue; do not follow that of sin. Virtue is the law to follow, and the virtuous person is said to rest in bliss.

entries.claim: Good people shine from afar, like the snowy mountains; bad people are not seen, like arrows shot by night.
entries.bears: Good people are compared to snowy mountains seen from far off.
entries.modern: Good people shine from afar, like the snowy mountains; bad people are not seen, like arrows shot by night. Good people are compared to snowy mountains seen from far off.

entries.claim: The twin verses make pain follow an evil thought and, in the next verse, happiness follow a pure one, as the wheel follows the ox.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The thought is the start of the consequence.
entries.modern: The twin verses make pain follow an evil thought and, in the next verse, happiness follow a pure one, as the wheel follows the ox. The thought is the start of the consequence.

entries.claim: Virtue is called a perfume above sandal and flower, and the hearer is told to take virtuous people, not evil-doers, for friends.
entries.loc: Chapters on flowers and the wise
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Company is part of the practice.
entries.modern: Virtue is called a perfume above sandal and flower, and the hearer is told to take virtuous people, not evil-doers, for friends. Company is part of the practice.

entries.claim: Later verses say to follow the law of virtue rather than sin, and that good people are seen from far away.
entries.loc: Chapters on the world and the path
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The law is something a person follows, not a mood.
entries.modern: Later verses say to follow the law of virtue rather than sin, and that good people are seen from far away. The law is something a person follows, not a mood.
